primary_claim: Running Claude Opus 4.6 autonomously overnight on a synthetic SAE benchmark (SynthSAEBench-16k), it discovered SAE architectural improvements -- including autonomously reviving a 2010 LISTA dictionary-learning algorithm as a Matryoshka SAE encoder -- that raised F1 from 0.88 to 0.97 (matching the logistic-regression-probe ceiling) and MCC from 0.78 to 0.84, though transfer of these improvements to real LLM SAEs remains unverified.

effect.metric: F1 score and MCC (cosine similarity to ground-truth features) on SynthSAEBench-16k

stated_future_work: Verify whether the discovered SAE architecture improvements transfer to LLM SAEs (via SAEBench)
Create a suite of synthetic models with varying properties to check the improvements aren't overfit to this specific synthetic model
Expand the quantity/quality of SAEBench datasets and obtain more compute to test ideas rigorously with multiple seeds
limitations_stated: Improvements have not yet been verified to transfer to real LLM SAEs; results on LLM SAEs via SAEBench have so far been mixed and inconclusive
SAEBench metrics are noisy, requiring multiple seeds and L0 values, and properly evaluating a single architecture change can cost $1000+ in compute
Claude tends to be overconfident in interpreting sprint results without considering alternative explanations, and can get anchored on the first ideas that work rather than exploring broadly
quote: By morning, it had boosted F1 score from 0.88 to 0.95.
